asserts: Bucket j at level K covers raw samples [j*BF^K, (j+1)*BF^K), anchored at global sample index 0 — never at a block boundary and never at a time — so block b at level K starts at raw sample b * BF^(K+1).
source: the anchored dyadic geometry, stated as arithmetic
contract: Bucket boundaries are anchored to the data rather than to a block or a time, which is what lets two implementations agree on them without negotiating.
notes: A block holds `block_samples` buckets rather than exactly BF, so the block-start column below is stated for block_samples == BF (today's geometry) and separately for block_samples == 2 * BF, which is the first value the parameter makes legal.
